traps.effect: An arc of electricity jumps between the tips of the staves the statues hold. Any creature in the path of the arc takes 11 (2d10) lightning damage and is stunned for 1 round. A successful DC 14 Dexterity saving throw halves the damage and negates the stunned condition.
traps.area: The path of the arc between the two statues
traps.description: Two bronze statues of robed, hooded figures carrying staves create an arc of electricity when a creature walks between them.

traps.name: Incense Trap
traps.trigger: Burning any of Durgleel's meditation incense

detection.detail: No detection method specified; the incense appears as innocuous herbs and weeds mixed with spores.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: Releases a cloud of toxic smoke. All creatures in the area of this smoke must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, creatures take 9 (2d8) poison damage and are poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned from the incense, a creature is plagued with "visions," vivid flashes of other places and events, which cause the creature to have disadvantage on attacks and on any Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based saving throws and skill checks for as long as they are poisoned. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and is not poisoned. Should any creature directly inhale the incense for whatever reason, they inhale some of the deadly spores. The DC of the saving throw is then increased to 16, the poison damage increases to 18 (4d8), and the poisoned duration increases to 10 minutes.
traps.area: Cloud of toxic smoke (area not specified)
traps.description: A sack of meditation incense mixed with deadly spores from Roggsothof the Fungal Horror. Burning it releases toxic smoke that poisons and plagues creatures with visions.

traps.name: Hall of Force Trap
traps.trigger: Each plate projects a powerful wave of energy any time a creature passes in front of it within 15 feet.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell will show an aura of evocation magic around each plate. A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check will provide a way to neutralize the magic of the plates for 1 minute, allowing passage without setting them off.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check will provide a way to neutralize the magic of the plates for 1 minute, allowing passage without setting them off.

traps.effect: A creature caught in a wave must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 11 (2d10) force damage and is pushed 15 feet and knocked prone. On a successful saving throw, the creature takes half damage, remains unmoved, and is not knocked prone. The first plate is only 10 feet from the opposite wall however, so a creature that fails its saving throw also takes 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage from its impact with the opposite wall before falling prone. A creature that fails its saving throw against the third plate must also succeed at a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or be knocked over the side of the bridge into the stream below.
traps.area: 15 feet in front of each plate
traps.description: Three large plates of a strange, blue-green metal mounted to the wall project powerful waves of energy at creatures passing in front of them.

traps.name: Deadfall Trap
traps.trigger: A tripwire is stretched across the passage leading up from the bottom of the sinkhole in Area 14, right at the top of the first incline before the passage widens. If triggered, a deadfall—a large log with sharpened spikes along the side facing the tripwire—drops from behind a dip in the ceiling, swinging from ropes attached to each end, to arc down into any creatures in the widest area of the passage to the top of the first incline where the tripwire is located.

detection.detail: A successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check will spot the camouflaged tripwire.

disarm.method: Avoid the trap or trigger from a safe distance
disarm.detail: The easiest method is to simply avoid the trap, stepping over the tripwire and moving on. Alternatively, the tripwire can be triggered from a safe distance. Once the trap is triggered, it will not go off again until reset, and the deadfall can either be cut down or bypassed.

traps.effect: The deadfall deals 22 (4d10) piercing damage to all creatures in its path and impales them on the spikes, where they are restrained. A successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw halves the damage and the creature is not restrained. If a creature beats the DC by 5 or more, it takes no damage at all and completely avoids the deadfall.
traps.area: The widest area of the passage to the top of the first incline where the tripwire is located
traps.description: A tripwire-triggered deadfall log with sharpened spikes that swings down from the ceiling to impale creatures in a passage.

traps.name: Collapsing Roof
traps.trigger: Whenever the walls or ceiling inside the estate are subject to a significant disturbance—such as a fireball spell or a Medium or larger creature being thrown into it
traps.effect: There is a 20% chance the roof in that 5-foot square, and in a 5-foot radius around it, collapses. Creatures caught in the collapse must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, all squares affected by the collapse become difficult terrain.
traps.area: 5-foot square and 5-foot radius around it
traps.description: The roof is less protected than the walls and has the potential to collapse.

traps.name: Control Panel
traps.trigger: Operating a lever, wheel, or switch on the control panel

detection.detail: The cabinet is clearly visible; its purpose is not obvious.

disarm.detail: No method given.

traps.effect: Roll d100 and consult the table: 01–25 No effect. 26–50 Insecticide sprays in Areas 10–15, but the concoction has weakened over time. Insects are not killed but enraged. Add one swarm of insects to each of those areas. If this result is rolled a second time, the second dose kills any swarms. This result has no effect after the second time. 51–60 A magical fertilizer is applied to Areas 6 and 10–15, causing rapid growth. All terrain in Areas 10–15 is now considered difficult terrain. Each plant creature in Areas 6 and 10–15 gain 11 (2d10) temporary hit points and a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls. If this result is rolled again, it has no effect. 61–70 A purifying element is released into the water in Areas 10–15. Acraecea's corrupt form is inadvertently affected, and she is poisoned for 1 hour. If this result is rolled again, it has no effect. 71–90 Herbicide is released into the test planter in Area 6, killing the quash moss (see Hazards in Appendix). 91–95 That particular lever/switch/wheel shorts out, causing smoke and dealing 11 (2d10) lightning damage to the creature that triggered it. 96–00 Same as a roll of 91–95, except the resulting feedback shorts out the entire machine, causing a cloud of smoke to fill the entire passageway for 1 minute, which heavily obscures the area and possibly alerts creatures in nearby areas to the PCs' presence, at GM's discretion.
traps.area: Areas 6, 10–15, or the creature that triggered it
traps.description: A strange metal cabinet affixed to the western wall, covered with levers, wheels, and switches. It was the control unit for experimental treatments the wizard had developed for his garden.

traps.name: Illusion-Shrouded Pit
traps.trigger: A creature steps onto the illusory floor covering the pit in the center of the room.

detection.detail: Anyone examining the floor carefully and succeeding on a DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check notices faint scratches on the floor outlining a rough square, just over 5 feet per side. Tactile investigation of the floor within the square reveals it to be nothing more than an illusion.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described in the source text.

traps.effect: A creature that falls into the pit takes half the normal falling damage since the decaying vegetation piled at the bottom softens the fall. A mass of asp vines lurks in the pile at the bottom of the pit and attacks any creature that falls into the pit, scoring it with their poisonous thorns until it dies.
traps.area: A 50-foot-deep pit, just over 5 feet per side, in the center of the room.
traps.description: A 50-foot-deep pit lies covered with an illusion to appear as a normal floor in the center of a small cave.

traps.name: Colored Paver Trap
traps.trigger: Stepping on any paver that is not pink, including walking toward the archway without specifying which paver is stepped on.

detection.detail: Only the pink stones are safe to walk upon; the danger is apparent from the color of the pavers.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is given; the trap is avoided by stepping only on pink pavers.

traps.effect: The creature takes 1d4 damage of a type according to the paver's color: necrotic (black), radiant (white), force (green), fire (red), acid (orange), and cold (blue).
traps.damage_type: varies (necrotic, radiant, force, fire, acid, or cold)
traps.area: The paved area leading to the center archway.
traps.description: A paved path where only pink stones are safe; stepping on any other color paver deals 1d4 damage of a type based on the paver's color.

traps.name: Collapsing Floor
traps.trigger: A character who weighs more than 150 pounds moves faster than half speed within Area 5.

detection.detail: The floor is visibly damaged, with a large portion of the southeast side fallen into the room below and holes in the ceiling.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is given; the trap is avoided by moving at half speed or less, or by weighing 150 pounds or less.

traps.effect: The floor collapses beneath the character, and they fall through to the room below, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage.
traps.area: Area 5: Destroyed Rooms.
traps.description: A weakened floor in the destroyed rooms that collapses under heavy or fast-moving characters, dropping them into the room below.

traps.name: Radiant Eye Tapestry
traps.trigger: PCs who investigate or look at the tapestry for more than 20 seconds

detection.detail: The tapestry depicting the radiant eye is saturated with mysterious, divine energy from years of intense and repentant prayer in front of it.

traps.effect: must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be paralyzed in ecstasy for 1d4 hours
traps.description: A tapestry depicting the radiant eye that paralyzes those who gaze upon it.

traps.name: Vomiting Slime Mold Trap
traps.trigger: When a creature opens the northern door, a barely contained flow of slime mold sprays out.

detection.detail: A successful DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check hears a gurgling sound behind the northern door as if a high-pressure fluid is pushing against it.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check when opening the door holds it open just enough for the pressure from the slime to be released without harming all creatures within 15 feet of the door. On a failure, the trap triggers as normal.

traps.effect: Each creature within 15 feet of the door must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 5 (1d10) bludgeoning damage and 11 (2d10) poison damage and is poisoned for 10 minutes. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't poisoned.
traps.area: 15 feet of the door
traps.description: A trap that sprays slime mold when the northern door is opened, dealing bludgeoning and poison damage and poisoning creatures.

traps.name: Violet Fungus Expulsion Trap
traps.trigger: When a creature opens the southern door, a wall of violet fungus explodes in rotting spores.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notices the smell of rot behind the southern door.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check when opening the door slows the flow of spores, limiting how many are ejected at one time. If successful, each creature within 20 feet of the door has advantage on its saving throw. On a failure, the trap triggers as normal. Alternatively, a gust of wind spell timed with opening the door disperses the spores harmlessly.

traps.effect: Each creature within 20 feet of the door must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: 20 feet of the door
traps.description: A trap that explodes with rotting spores when the southern door is opened, dealing necrotic damage.

traps.name: Stuck and Hidden Trapdoor
traps.trigger: Attempting to open the trapdoor

detection.detail: A successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check locates the trapdoor. Alternatively, the PCs can discover the trapdoor by spending 20 minutes, clearing the rubble from the room.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check pulls open the stuck trapdoor.

traps.effect: The trapdoor is stuck and must be forced open.
traps.description: A concealed trapdoor in a debris-strewn room that is stuck and must be forced open.

traps.name: Maddening Statue
traps.trigger: A PC spends more than 1 round inspecting the statue

detection.detail: The effigy's worn state makes it difficult to discern any details about the deity, but the PCs can make out the remains of whorls and eyes carved all over the statue.

traps.effect: The PC must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be afflicted with a short-term madness for 1 minute. If an affected PC hits an unaffected creature, that creature must also succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be afflicted with a short-term madness for 1 minute. A creature so afflicted with a short-term madness can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
traps.area: Single creature inspecting the statue; secondary creatures hit by an affected PC
traps.description: An eroded effigy to an ancient god of insanity whose worn state hides whorls and eyes carved all over it. Inspecting it too long afflicts viewers with short-term madness.

traps.name: Poison Darts Trap
traps.trigger: A pressure plate just inside the doors
traps.effect: Setting off the trap summons the two shadow fey guardians (see Tome of Beasts) to Area 6.
traps.area: Area 3: Southeast Entrance Interior
traps.description: A pressure plate just inside the doors triggers a poison darts trap. Setting off the trap summons the two shadow fey guardians (see Tome of Beasts) to Area 6.

traps.name: The Trapped Path
traps.trigger: Stepping on an incorrect tile in the hallway

detection.detail: A spell such as detect magic, or other effect that can sense magic, reveals an abjuration aura around the tiles.

disarm.detail: The magic of the tiles can't be dispelled until the darkness covering the compound disperses and sunlight shines on the hills again.

traps.effect: Each creature in the room must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one as it is wreathed in ghostly flames. All tiles in the room cease to glow, the trap activates, and the path resets.
traps.area: The entire hallway (Path of Contemplation)
traps.description: A meditative path of eight painted moon-phase tiles that doubles as a deadly trap. To open the doors at the far end, PCs must walk on the correct tiles in the correct order.

traps.name: Path of Fire
traps.trigger: A character walks across the hot coals.

detection.detail: The hot coals are plainly visible.

disarm.detail: No disarm method provided.

traps.effect: The character takes fire damage.
traps.area: A 10-foot path of hot coals.
traps.description: A 10-foot path of hot coals that burns those who walk across it.

traps.name: Icy Water
traps.trigger: A character walks through the shallow, icy water.

detection.detail: The icy water is plainly visible.

disarm.detail: No disarm method provided.

traps.effect: The character's speed is halved until they finish a short rest by a fire (or other source of prolonged warmth).
traps.area: A small stretch of icy water.
traps.description: A small stretch of icy water that chills those who walk through it.

traps.name: Crumbling Bridge
traps.trigger: When a creature walks across the center of the bridge

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Survival) check finds a set of tracks that appear to follow a safe path across the bridge.

disarm.detail: No disarm method given; creatures on the safe path don't trigger the trap.

traps.effect: The creature falls to the ground 20 feet below as part of the bridge gives way. The creature takes 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone and buried under the rubble below the bridge. The buried target is restrained and unable to breathe or stand up. A creature can take an action to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, ending the buried state on a success.
traps.area: Center of the stone bridge between Area 4 and Area 6
traps.description: A damaged stone bridge that gives way when walked across, dropping creatures 20 feet into rubble.

traps.name: Sands of Sleep
traps.trigger: Any character who touches the sleeping sand

detection.detail: The pit is filled with white sand that continuously churns like ocean waves; objects can be glimpsed bubbling to the surface.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed; characters must avoid contact or be pulled out.

traps.effect: Any character who touches the sand must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious. An unconscious PC is rapidly pulled underneath the sand and begins to suffocate. An unconscious character can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns to see if they wake up. Pulling a character out of the sand or swimming out of the sand requires a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
traps.area: A lake of white sand beneath a thin walkway between two doors.
traps.description: A pit of sleeping sand that causes unconsciousness and suffocation to those who touch it.

traps.name: Forever Hall Teleportation Trap
traps.trigger: If either door is entered, it will swing shut 2 rounds after a creature passes over its threshold. A creature entering the square in front of either of the doors will be teleported to the center of the hallway.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the door beyond the illusion. A detect magic spell will note illusion magic in the hallway, conjuration magic at the two true ends of the hall, and abjuration magic from the glass globes above.

disarm.detail: Damaging the mosaic on the floor in front of the doors will disable the teleportation effect. The squares have an AC 15. Doing at least 14 damage to the tiles is enough to disable the teleportation effect in that square.

traps.effect: The hallway seems to lengthen with the door at the far end receding into the distance. No matter how fast a creature runs the length of the hallway, they never seem to get any closer to the door. Looking in the other direction, back to the entrance, reveals a similar lengthening of the hallway. The lengthening of the hall is an illusion, and the reason a creature can never reach the end of the hall is because a creature entering the square in front of either of the doors will be teleported to the center of the hallway.
traps.area: The hallway between the two doors, about 20 feet long.
traps.description: A magical trap in a hallway that creates an illusion of an endlessly lengthening hall and teleports creatures who step in front of either door back to the center.

traps.name: Snow Pits
traps.trigger: When a creature steps anywhere in the pit's 10-foot square, the layer of snow gives way.

detection.detail: A successful DC 19 Wisdom (Perception) or DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check alerts a character to a pit's presence and allows them to walk around it.

disarm.detail: Topping a pit with a stout tarp or other covering allows free movement across the pit.

traps.effect: The layer of snow gives way, dumping the creature 30 feet into the pit below unless it succeeds on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. The pit's walls are sheer ice, requiring a trapped creature to succeed on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check to scale.
traps.area: 10-foot square, 30 feet deep
traps.description: Three snow pits randomly placed 20–30 feet from the pass's entrance await the unwary.

traps.name: Falling Icicles
traps.trigger: Sound and vibration dislodge the icicles, which impale those below. Anything above whispered conversation disturbs them as does walking heavily.

detection.detail: A successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check or DC 17 Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) check realizes the icicles' inherent danger.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals that a spell or effect that deals thunder damage causes the icicles to fall, rendering the area harmless afterward. A success by 5 or more also informs the character that the area of effect for such a spell or effect increases by 50%.

traps.effect: A creature passing through the area must make a DC 16 passive Dexterity (Stealth) check. On a failure, 1d4 icicles fall on the creature. Each icicle makes a ranged attack with a +9 bonus. If an icicle hits the creature, the target takes 9 (2d8) piercing damage and 4 (1d8) cold damage. If a creature fails the check by 5 or more, all creatures within 10 feet of the creature are subject to the above attacks.
traps.area: Area of the forest with icicles; 10-foot radius on severe failure
traps.description: Inches-long icicles hang from the trees in this forest and lightly chime as they sway in the breeze. The cult maintains this section of the forest, with its dangerous, spear-like icicles, as it provides the most direct route to Havenhearth.

traps.name: Rockfall
traps.trigger: A lever in Area 10 of the lower level triggers this trap. Alternatively, a successful DC 16 Dexterity (thieves' tools) check opens the hatch, albeit unsafely.

detection.detail: A successful DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the hatch.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 19 Dexterity (thieves' tools) check jams the hatch mechanism, rendering the lever useless.

traps.effect: When the rocks are released, they completely fill the 10-foot corridor, crushing everything within. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage and is both prone and restrained. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and is not otherwise affected. A creature, or any adjacent creature, can take its action to free itself with a successful DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check.
traps.area: 10-foot corridor
traps.description: A concealed hatch blocks several hundred pounds of loose rocks, triggered by a lever in Area 10 of the lower level.

traps.name: Glyph of Warding (Pyroclastic Burst)
traps.trigger: If the door is opened without speaking the phrase "Mother is expecting me," it triggers a pyroclastic burst spell centered on the creature that triggered the glyph.

detection.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check uncovers the glyph etched on the door's center. Detect magic or another such spell reveals the glyph's abjuration aura.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 14) cast on the door destroys the glyph.

traps.effect: Triggers a pyroclastic burst spell (save DC 18) centered on the creature that triggered the glyph.
traps.area: Centered on the creature that triggered the glyph
traps.description: The door is trapped with a glyph of warding that triggers a pyroclastic burst spell if the door is opened without speaking the passphrase.

traps.name: Pit Trap
traps.trigger: When a creature steps in one of the areas denoted by the X on the map, the trap activates.

detection.detail: A successful DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check notices the incongruities in the floor.

traps.effect: The creature must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or fall 15 feet into a lava-heated pit. At the beginning of each of its turns, the creature takes 4 (1d8) fire damage.
traps.area: Areas denoted by the X on the map
traps.description: A hidden pit trap in the storeroom that drops victims into a lava-heated pit.

traps.name: Shadow Tendrils
traps.trigger: A creature touches the shadow river or ends its turn within 10 feet of it
traps.effect: Takes 5 (2d4) necrotic damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have its Strength score reduced by 1d4. The creature dies if this reduces its Strength to 0. Otherwise, the reduction lasts until the creature finishes a short or long rest. A humanoid that dies from this damage or Strength reduction rises as a shadow under the shadow river lord's control after 1 minute.
traps.area: Within 10 feet of the shadow river
traps.description: The shadow river poses a threat to creatures not native to the Shadow Realm or granted protection by the Weft of Shadows.

traps.name: Quash Moss
traps.trigger: Pressure applied to its surface, as when a creature walks upon it

detection.detail: Appears as completely normal moss until pressure is applied to its surface

disarm.detail: Any effect that causes fire damage or 48 hours of exposure to direct sunlight will destroy an average patch of quash moss.

traps.effect: The moss curls up, wrapping around whatever is on it. A creature must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw to jump clear; otherwise, the quash moss rolls up tightly around it. A captured creature is restrained and takes 5 (1d10) bludgeoning damage and 5 (1d10) acid damage each round on its turn. A captured creature may make a DC 13 Dexterity check each round, slipping free on a success.
traps.area: 10-foot square
traps.description: This thick, deep-green moss grows quickly after a spawning storm, typically in shaded areas. A typical patch of quash moss covers a 10-foot square.
